communication_guide.overview: Guidelines for providing constructive, actionable feedback to developers during code review. Focus on code, not the person who wrote it.

principle.name: Focus on Code, Not Person
principle.description: Direct all feedback toward the code and implementation, not toward the developer. Avoid personal attacks or criticism.

examples.good: "The function could benefit from early returns to avoid unnecessary processing" "Consider using a Set for better lookup performance"
examples.bad: "You wrote this wrong" (personal attack) "This is sloppy code" (personal criticism)

principle.name: Be Specific and Actionable
principle.description: Provide clear, specific feedback with exact locations. Include actionable steps for remediation. Avoid vague suggestions.

examples.good: "Line 42 in src/auth/login.ts has a potential null reference. Consider adding a null check: `if (user) { return user; }`" "The email validation regex at line 15 doesn't validate international email addresses. Update to: `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/i`"
examples.bad: "This code looks wrong" (too vague) "Fix the error handling" (not specific) "Make it better" (not actionable)

principle.name: Explain the "Why", Not Just "What"
principle.description: When identifying issues, explain the impact and potential consequences. Help developers understand the importance of the fix.

examples.good: "This SQL injection vulnerability could allow attackers to access all user data. Consider using parameterized queries to prevent this." "Missing error handling here could cause the application to crash when the API returns an error. Add a try-catch block."
examples.bad: "This is bad practice" (no explanation) "Don't do this" (no context)

principle.name: Provide Code Examples
principle.description: Show both the problematic code and the corrected version. This helps developers understand the expected pattern.

principle.name: Balance Strictness with Context
principle.description: Maintain high quality standards but consider project context, deadlines, and the nature of the change. Be reasonable about minor issues that don't affect functionality.

examples.good: "For a hotfix addressing a critical bug, focus on the fix. For a new feature, provide more comprehensive feedback." "This naming convention violation is minor given the larger refactoring in progress. Note it for future reference."
examples.bad: "Reject everything for minor issues" (too strict) "Accept everything without comment" (too lenient)

principle.name: Use Severity Levels Appropriately
principle.description: Categorize issues by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low) to help developers prioritize fixes. Be consistent with your severity ratings.

level.name: CRITICAL
level.description: Security vulnerabilities, data loss risks, crashes, test failures
level.action: Block commit and push, require immediate fix

level.name: HIGH
level.description: Performance issues, logic errors, missing test coverage
level.action: Should be fixed before merge, can be noted for later

level.name: MEDIUM
level.description: Code style violations, minor improvements, suggestions
level.action: Can be noted for future, optional to fix now

critique_structure.overview: Use a consistent structure for all review critiques to ensure clarity and completeness.

section.name: Summary
section.content: Total files reviewed Overall assessment (Pass/Fail) Critical issues count High/Medium/Low issues count

section.name: Critical Issues
section.content: For each critical issue: - Issue title - Location (file:line) - Severity - Description - Impact - Required action

section.name: High Priority Issues
section.content: For each high priority issue: - Issue title - Location (file:line) - Severity - Description - Suggested remediation

section.name: Medium Priority Issues
section.content: For each medium priority issue: - Issue title - Location (file:line) - Severity - Description - Suggested remediation (optional)

section.name: Low Priority Issues
section.content: For each low priority issue: - Issue title - Location (file:line) - Severity - Description - Suggestion (optional)

section.name: Positive Feedback
section.content: - Strengths observed - Good practices followed - Commendations

section.name: Next Steps
section.content: - Required fixes (with priority) - Suggested improvements (with priority) - Actions before re-review

template.name: critical_security_issue
template.description: Template for reporting critical security vulnerabilities
template.content:
## CRITICAL: [Issue Title]
**Location:** [file]:[line]
**Description:** [Clear description of vulnerability]
**Impact:** [Explain potential consequences]
**Required Action:** 1. [Specific remediation step 1] 2. [Specific remediation step 2] 3. [Additional steps as needed]
**This issue MUST be fixed before any code can be committed.**
---

template.name: high_priority_issue
template.description: Template for reporting high priority issues
template.content:
## HIGH: [Issue Title]
**Location:** [file]:[line]
**Description:** [Clear description of issue]
**Suggested Remediation:** [Specific fix approach with code example if helpful]
---

template.name: medium_priority_issue
template.description: Template for reporting medium priority issues
template.content:
## MEDIUM: [Issue Title]
**Location:** [file]:[line]
**Description:** [Clear description of issue]
**Suggested Remediation:** (optional) [Suggested improvement or fix]
---

template.name: low_priority_note
template.description: Template for low priority informational notes

template.name: full_review_pass
template.content:
## Code Review: APPROVED ✓
**Files Reviewed:** [count] files **Tests:** [count] tests passed
**Assessment:** All quality and security checks passed
**Commit Message:** [Conventional commit message generated]
**Action:** Changes staged, committed, and pushed to repository
---

template.name: full_review_fail
template.content:
## Code Review: REQUIRES FIX ✗
**Files Reviewed:** [count] files **Tests:** [count] tests passed
**Issues Found:** - Critical: [count] - High: [count] - Medium: [count] - Low: [count]
**Action Required:** Please address the issues above before re-review.
**Next Steps:** 1. Fix critical issues 2. Address high priority issues 3. Update tests if needed 4. Request re-review
---

scenario.name: security_vulnerability_found
scenario.description: When a critical security issue is discovered
scenario.approach: Immediately halt the review process. Do not run tests. Do not stage, commit, or push any changes. Provide detailed critique with severity clearly marked as CRITICAL. Explain the potential impact and consequences. Provide specific remediation steps with code examples.

scenario.name: test_failure
scenario.approach: Identify which test is failing and why. Check if it's a test issue or code issue. Provide specific guidance on fixing the test or the code. Do not proceed until tests pass.

scenario.name: code_standards_violation
scenario.approach: Reference the specific standard or convention being violated. Explain why the standard exists and its importance. Provide the corrected code or pattern. Mark as MEDIUM priority unless it affects functionality.

scenario.name: missing_documentation
scenario.approach: Identify what documentation is missing (JSDoc, comments, README). Explain the importance of documentation for maintainability. Request appropriate documentation be added. Mark as LOW priority if code is otherwise sound.

scenario.name: performance_concerns
scenario.approach: Explain the performance impact and why it matters. Provide specific optimization suggestions with code examples. Mark as HIGH priority if it affects production performance. Consider if optimization is urgent or can be deferred.

scenario.name: successful_review
scenario.description: When all checks pass and code is approved
scenario.approach: Summarize the positive aspects of the code. Confirm all tests passed with coverage metrics. Generate conventional commit message following project standards. Stage all changed files. Create commit with the message. Push to repository. Confirm successful push with commit hash.
